subject.title: fix(sessions): sweep orphan store temp files

question: Should stale matching session-store temp files be deleted during ordinary session-store load/cache miss, or should deletion remain limited to explicit cleanup and disk-budget flows?
rationale: This is a session-state deletion boundary: the source evidence supports the leak and the PR is narrow, but only maintainers can decide whether automatic load-time filesystem cleanup is acceptable for production session directories.

options.title: Accept Load-Time Cleanup
options.body: Refresh the branch, keep the basename-aware stale-temp guard, and proceed with merge validation for the automatic sweep.

options.title: Require Shared Cleanup Rule First
options.body: Ask for the five-minute stale-temp policy to be factored through the existing disk-budget cleanup rule before merge.

options.title: Keep Cleanup Explicit Only
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers want stale temp deletion limited to doctor, sessions cleanup, or disk-budget paths.

recommendation.title: Accept Load-Time Cleanup
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, keep the basename-aware stale-temp guard, and proceed with merge validation for the automatic sweep.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the precursor session-temp cleanup PR and is the strongest available routing candidate for accepting or rejecting the production cleanup boundary.
